statements.claim: A weeping man runs to Krishna's chariot crying 'Krishna, Krishna, mighty-armed one! Your father — you who love your father!' and reports that Shalva has broken into Dwaraka and carried off Vasudeva like an animal.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.21-22 (krsna krsna maha-baho pita te pitr-vatsala); pack excerpt: 'A man appears weeping and tells Krishna that Shalva has carried off his father Vasudeva like an animal.'

statements.claim: Krishna had hurried back from Indraprastha after omens of danger reached him during his cousin's great sacrifice, and found Shalva attacking with the flying city Saubha; since his return they had fought a running duel across the sea.
statements.evidence: Corpus chain (DKS_0403): 'Returning from Indraprastha and seeing evil omens, Krishna hurries to Dwaraka... and joins the fight'; MB 3.21 duel narrative in pack.

statements.claim: Shalva hurled iron javelins, flaming lances and heavy clubs, and Krishna cut each into two or three pieces so the sea rained splinters.
statements.evidence: MB 3.21 (pack): 'that wicked one hurled at me Sataghnis, and mighty maces, and flaming lances, and stout clubs... I speedily resisted them with my swift arrows, and cut them in two or three pieces.'

statements.claim: Krishna hurled his mace at Shalva; when it came spinning back, the sky where Shalva had stood was empty and his war-cries came from everywhere.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.19-20: struck Shalva with his mace of terrible velocity; when the mace returned (gadayam sannivrttayam) Shalva disappeared (salvas tv antaradhīyata).

statements.claim: Shalva then appeared holding an old man in Vasudeva's robes, taunted 'Here is your father!... Save him, if you can!', and beheaded the old man before Krishna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.25-26: 'esa te janita tato yad-artham iha jivasi' and Shalva (mayavi) strikes with his sword; pack excerpt: 'Shalva then seems to behead Vasudeva before Krishna, taunting him to save him if he can.'

statements.claim: For a moment Krishna took on the human mood and was grief-stricken, thinking only of the fallen father.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.22,27: nisamya vipriyam krsno manusim prakrtim gatah; 'tato muhurtam prakrtav upaplutah sva-bodha aste sva-jananusangatah' — for a moment overwhelmed by attachment, he remained absorbed in his own awareness.

statements.claim: Looking again, Krishna saw no messenger, no body, no head, no blood — only the sky with Saubha — and perceived it was the demon's sorcery, Maya; the father he had mourned was safe and the death had never happened.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.28: 'na tatra dutam na pituh kalevaram prabuddha ajau samapasyad acyutah' (no messenger, no father's corpse); pack excerpt: 'perceives it to be the demon's sorcery wrought by Maya.'

statements.claim: Krishna raised his bow again and the real battle resumed.
statements.evidence: MB 3.21 (pack): 'recovering my senses, I again began to discharge arrows by hundreds.'

notes: Battlefield recap (Indraprastha omens, sea duel, Dwaraka 'undefended') is connective recap of the DKS_0403 chain; 'every man in that host knew the report was possible' is inner-state atmosphere, not a factual assertion contradicted by the pack.

statements.claim: Shalva came down one final time rushing at Krishna, and Krishna met him with arrows that pierced his guard, cut through his armor, snapped his bow, and tore the jewel from his crest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.32 (pack excerpt): 'Krishna pierces the rushing Shalva with arrows, cuts through his armor, bow and crest-jewel.'

statements.claim: Krishna's own horses and charioteer Daruka had earlier stood thick with shafts; the pierced and enfeebled Daruka confessed he could barely hold the reins, and Krishna cheered him, telling him the driver's duty was to stay at the reins.
statements.evidence: MB 3.21 (full text quoted in the DKS_0404 evidence pack of the same Shalva battle): 'Salwa covered Daruka, and my steeds, and my car... with hundreds of straight shafts'; Daruka: 'My body hath become weak!'; 'seeing the charioteer... pierced and enfeebled by the shafts of Salwa... I cheered him up.' Detail belongs to the same duel narrative; not present in DKS_0405's own excerpted passages.

statements.claim: Krishna took up his mace and turned it on the city; Saubha came apart and fell into the water in a thousand fragments, swallowed by the sea.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.33 (pack): 'tat krsna-hasteritaya vicurnitam papata toye gadaya sahasradha' — shattered by the mace hurled from Krishna's hand it fell into the water in a thousand fragments; pack excerpt agrees.

statements.claim: Men would say Saubha went down as Tripura had gone down of old, the triple city shaken from the sky by the great god's shafts.
statements.evidence: MB excerpt in pack: 'it fell like the city of Tripura shaken by the shafts of Maheswara.'

statements.claim: With the city gone, Shalva came at Krishna on foot, mace in hand, and as he rushed in Krishna severed the arm that held the mace.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.34: 'adhavatah sa-gadam tasya bahum bhallena chittva' — severing the arm of the rushing, mace-bearing Shalva.

statements.claim: Krishna raised the discus, which blazed like the sun at the end of the world, and it cut off Shalva's crowned head; where it passed, the enemy burned.
statements.evidence: BP 10.77.35 (pack excerpt): 'wielding his wondrous discus blazing like the sun at world's end, cuts off his crowned head'; MB excerpt: 'with its energy it set the foe ablaze.'

statements.claim: The war was over: the sea smoothed over the scattered stones of Saubha and the sky above Dwaraka was only sky again.
statements.evidence: Closing imagery consistent with the pack's account of Saubha's destruction; phrasing is atmospheric, not a discrete sourceable event.

notes: Two pack quirks noted: (1) the MB 'passage' quoted under DKS_0405 (3.23) is forest-departure text, but the pack's MB excerpt lines correctly describe the discus cutting Saubha and cleaving Salwa — story follows the BP variant (mace shatters city), matching the pack's own summary; (2) the Daruka anecdote is supported by MB 3.21, quoted in full in the adjacent DKS_0404 evidence pack for the same battle.

statements.claim: On the road home from the war with Shalva, the ground began to shake and a single figure — Dantavakra, mace in hand — approached on foot.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.1: 'ekah padatih sankruddho gada-panih prakampayan' — alone, on foot, angry, mace in hand, making the earth tremble; pack excerpt: Dantavakra 'rushes at Krishna on foot.'

statements.claim: Dantavakra, kin to the slain Shishupala and friend to the slain Shalva, had come from his kingdom of Karusha to settle the debt of his slain friends, alone and on foot.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.3 (kārūṣaḥ = king of Karusha) and excerpt: 'Dantavakra, eager to repay his slain friends'; pack summary: attacks 'to avenge Shishupala and Shalva'; verse 4 'tvam matuleyo nah' makes both cousins of Krishna.

statements.claim: Krishna took up his own mace, Kaumodaki, and waited.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.2 ('gadam adaya satvarah'); pack excerpt names 'his mace Kaumodaki.'

statements.claim: Dantavakra taunted Krishna as a betrayer of friends and kinsman-killer — 'You are our own cousin... you turn on your own kin... I owe my friends a debt... I have come to pay it with your head.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.4-6: 'tvam matuleyo nah krsna mitra-dhrung mam jighamsasi / tarhy anrnyam upaimy ajna mitranam mitra-vatsalah' — cousin, betrayer of friends, repaying his debt to friends; killing Shishupala (at the rajasuya) and Shalva is chain-supported context (DKS_0401-0405).

statements.claim: His words were harsh as goads on an elephant, and Krishna heard them without a word.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.6: 'evam ruksais tudan vakyaih krsnam totrair iva dvipam' — goading Krishna with harsh words like goads on an elephant.

statements.claim: Dantavakra's mace came down on Krishna's head, but Krishna did not move, as though the blow had fallen on a mountain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.7: 'gadayabhihato 'py ajau na cacala yadudvahah' — though struck by the mace in battle the Yadu chief did not stir; pack excerpt: 'strikes him on the head with his mace. Unshaken, Krishna...'

statements.claim: Kaumodaki struck Dantavakra square in the chest and crushed it; he staggered, blood pouring from his mouth, and fell, and a subtle, wonderful light rose out of him and entered Krishna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.8-9: 'gada-nirbhinna-hrdaya udvaman rudhiram mukhat' (heart shattered by the mace, vomiting blood from the mouth); 'tatah suksmataram jyotih krsnam avisad adbhutam' (then a most subtle light wonderfully entered Krishna).

statements.claim: Viduratha, Dantavakra's brother, grief-stricken, rushed at Krishna, who severed his crowned head with the razor-edged discus.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.10-11: 'vidurathas tu tad-bhrata bhratr-soka-pariplutah'; 'krsnas cakrena ksura-nemina' — Krishna cut off his head with the razor-edged discus; pack excerpt: 'severs his crowned head with the discus.'

notes: Setting details ('Dwaraka's walls still a day's march ahead', 'no one on the road') are connective; closing reflections on the light and on vengeance are interpretive, not sourceable facts asserted as events.

statements.claim: In the hall of the Kurus at Hastinapura, Yudhishthira staked his wealth, kingdom, brothers one by one, then himself, and finally Draupadi, losing her too.
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): herald tells Draupadi 'The king had first staked his brothers, then himself, and then thee.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana commanded the herald (Pratikamin): 'Go, bring Draupadi here. You have nothing to fear from the sons of Pandu.'
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): 'Go Pratikamin, and bring thou Draupadi hither. Thou hast no fear from the sons of Pandu.'

statements.claim: The herald went unwillingly, like a dog entering a lion's den, and told Draupadi she had been won and must come to Dhritarashtra's house for menial work.
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): 'like a dog in a lion's den'; 'Yudhishthira having been intoxicated with dice, Duryodhana, O Draupadi, hath won thee... put thee in some menial work.'

statements.claim: Draupadi asked what prince stakes his wife, and sent the herald back to ask the gambler whom he lost first — himself or her.
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): 'What prince is there who playeth staking his wife?... ask that gambler... whom he hath lost first, himself, or me.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira sat like one demented, deprived of reason, and gave no answer good or ill.
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): 'Yudhishthira, however sat there like one demented and deprived of reason and gave no answer good or ill to the Suta.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana summoned Draupadi to put her question in the assembly; on the herald's second visit she answered that morality is the one highest object in the world and she would obey whatever the virtuous elders decided.
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): Duryodhana: 'Let the princess of Panchala come hither and put her question'; Draupadi: 'Morality, however, it hath been said, is the one highest object in the world... I am ready to do what those elderly and virtuous persons... will definitely tell me.'

statements.claim: The kings and elders sat with faces downward, none speaking, knowing the eagerness and resolution of Dhritarashtra's son; Yudhishthira sent word that she should go before her father-in-law and weep.
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): 'all sat with faces downwards, uttering not a word, knowing the eagerness and resolution of Dhritarashtra's son'; Yudhishthira 'sent a trusted messenger unto Draupadi, directing... she should come before her father-in-law weeping bitterly.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana then sent Dussasana — 'this herald fears Bhima. Go yourself, and bring the daughter of Yajnasena here by force' — and Dussasana, eyes red as blood, told her 'you have been won by us, and won rightly. Accept the Kurus for your lords.'
statements.evidence: MB 2.66 (pack): Duryodhana: 'this son of my Suta... feareth Vrikodara. Therefore, go thou thyself and forcibly bring hither the daughter of Yajnasena'; Dussasana 'rose with blood-red eyes... 'Come, come, O Krishna... thou hast been won by us... come now and accept the Kurus for thy lords.''

statements.claim: When she would not come, Dussasana seized her and dragged her into the hall before the gathered kings and began to strip her in the sight of all.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary and canonical event (evt_0400): 'As Dussasana drags her before the assembly and strips her, Draupadi cries out...'; MB passage shows Dussasana entering her abode and forcing her before the assembly.

statements.claim: Draupadi cried out to Govinda dwelling in Dwaraka, Krishna fond of the cowherds of Vrindavan, Kesava, husband of Lakshmi, lord of Vraja, destroyer of afflictions, Janardana — to rescue her from the Kaurava ocean.
statements.evidence: MB excerpt in pack: 'O Govinda, O thou who dwellest in Dwaraka, O Krishna, O thou who art fond of cow-herdesses... O Kesava, seest thou not that the Kauravas are humiliating me... O Janarddana, rescue me who am sinking in the Kaurava Ocean.'

statements.claim: She called past the assembly and her bound husbands, to the one name that could cross the distance toward the city by the sea.
statements.evidence: Poetic framing of the prayer; no discrete factual assertion beyond the supported cry itself.

notes: The interpretive sentence on the legal hinge of Draupadi's question ('a man who does not own himself cannot stake his wife') is framing consistent with the passage; closing paragraph is connective atmosphere.

statements.claim: In the Pandava camp at Upaplavya before the war, Yudhishthira spoke for peace; Sahadeva and the mighty car-warrior Satyaki approved, and Bhima too declared for peace; then Draupadi rose to address Krishna.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack): 'king Drupada's daughter Krishna... applauding Sahadeva and that mighty car-warrior Satyaki, addressed Madhava seated by his side. And beholding Bhimasena declare for peace, that intelligent lady... said.'

statements.claim: Draupadi spoke holding her dishevelled tresses, her black lotus-leaf eyes wet with tears.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'Draupadi, clutching her dishevelled hair'; MB 5.82 (pack): 'of eyes that were black in hue and large like lotus leaves, bathed in tears'; excerpt: 'call to thy mind these tresses of mine seized by Dussasana's rude hands.'

statements.claim: She recalled that the Pandavas had asked only for five villages — Avishthala, Vrikasthala, Makandi, Varanavata, and any fifth — via the message privately delivered to Sanjaya, and Duryodhana would not grant even that.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack), near-verbatim list of the five villages and the private message to Sanjaya; 'Suyodhana hath not acted according to them.'

statements.claim: She argued that if Duryodhana wanted peace only with the kingdom surrendered there was no need for Krishna to travel to Hastinapura; the Pandavas with the Srinjayas could withstand the Dhritarashtra host, and men unwinnable by conciliation or gifts must be met with severity.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack): 'there is no necessity of going thither for making such a peace. The Pandavas with the Srinjayas... are quite able to withstand the fierce Dhritarashtra host'; 'should be treated with severity.'

statements.claim: She urged that a Kshatriya true to his order must strike the covetous, with only a Brahmana excepted as preceptor of all orders, and that there is as much sin in sparing one who deserves death as in slaying one who does not.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack): 'He that is covetous... ought surely to be slain by a Kshatriya... The exception in the case of a Brahmana...'; 'there is equal sin in not slaying one that deserveth to be slain.'

statements.claim: She recounted her identity — daughter of Drupada risen from the sacrificial altar, sister of Dhrishtadyumna, daughter-in-law of Pandu, queen of his five sons, mother of five sons bound to Krishna as Abhimanyu was — and how she was seized by the hair, dragged into the assembly and treated as a slave in Krishna's own lifetime.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack), matching the identity catalogue and 'I was seized by the hair, dragged into the assembly and insulted in the very sight of the sons of Pandu and in thy life-time... treated as a slave.'

statements.claim: She reminded him how the brothers sat silent while she called on him in her heart ('Save me, O save me!'), how Dhritarashtra offered a boon and she asked only that the Pandavas be freed with cars and weapons, and how they were freed only to be exiled to the woods.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack): 'in my heart I called upon thee, O Govinda... Save me, O save me!'; 'Let the Pandavas be free men with their cars and weapons'; 'were freed but only to be exiled into the woods.'

statements.claim: She cried 'Fie to Arjuna's bowmanship and fie to Bhima's might, since Duryodhana lives even for a moment,' and asked that his wrath be directed at the sons of Dhritarashtra.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack): 'Fie to Partha's bowmanship, oh, fie to Bhimasena's might since Duryodhana, O Krishna, liveth for even a moment... let thy wrath, O Krishna, be directed towards the sons of Dhritarashtra.'

statements.claim: Weeping, walking like a cow-elephant, she came and stood before Krishna, waiting for his answer.
statements.evidence: MB 5.82 (pack): 'bathed in tears, and walking like a cow-elephant, approached the lotus-eyed [Krishna].'

notes: Her plea to inflict punishment 'with the Pandavas and the Srinjayas' and the 'son of Pritha' glory clause are direct paraphrases of the passage; no unsupported or contradicted factual claims found.

statements.claim: Krishna comforted the weeping Draupadi at Upaplavya, telling her she would soon behold the ladies of Bharata's race weeping as she wept, with their husbands and kinsmen slain.
statements.evidence: MB excerpt in pack: 'Soon wilt thou, O Krishna, behold the ladies of Bharata's race weep as thou dost'; index summary: 'swears that the women of the Kuru race will soon weep as she does, with their kinsmen slain.'

statements.claim: He swore that the mountains of Himavat might shift, the earth might split into a hundred fragments, but his words could never be futile.
statements.evidence: MB excerpt in pack: 'The mountains of Himavat might shift their site, the Earth herself might split into a hundred fragments... still my words can never be futile.'

statements.claim: He told her to dry her tears and swore she would soon see her husbands with their enemies slain.
statements.evidence: MB excerpt in pack: 'Stop thy tears, I swear to thee, O Krishna, soon wilt thou see thy husbands, with their enemies slain.'

statements.claim: Her appeal recapped the five villages refused, the seizure by the hair and dragging into the assembly, her cry 'save me, O save me', and freedom that ended in exile.
statements.evidence: Recap of the preceding DKS_0409 episode; every element matches MB 5.82 passage quoted in the pack.

statements.claim: The promise would be answered in the fate of the whole Kuru line: the men who wagered her would fall and their wives would weep as she had.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (Krishna: Kuru ladies 'weep as thou dost... with their enemies slain') and index summary; story's elaboration is faithful paraphrase.

statements.claim: The men present recalled that his word had held before in that assembly hall, when her robes streamed out endlessly and no hand could strip her.
statements.evidence: Corpus chain reference to DKS_0408 'Krishna Protects Draupadi with Endless Robes'; allusion, consistent with the corpus narrative.

notes: MB 5.82 passage displayed in the pack is Draupadi's preceding speech; Krishna's comforting vow is carried by the pack's excerpt of the same chapter. Metaphors ('the two were of the same fabric', 'settled like a stone') are connective.

statements.claim: At Upaplavya the brothers gathered around Krishna and pressed him to carry their cause to Hastinapura; Bhima and Nakula each spoke entrusting the family's hope to him before Arjuna rose.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'Bhima, Arjuna and Nakula each address Krishna, urging him to seek peace with the Kauravas and entrusting their cause to him.' (No speeches of Bhima/Nakula are quoted in the pack passage, which contains only Arjuna's words; the story gives them no quoted content either.)

statements.claim: Arjuna said Yudhishthira had already said what should be said, but that Krishna seemed not to think peace easily obtainable — whether from Dhritarashtra's covetousness or the Pandavas' present weakness — and that nothing should be regarded as impracticable.
statements.evidence: MB 5.78 (pack), close paraphrase of Arjuna's opening.

statements.claim: Arjuna urged Krishna to strive for peace, as the foremost friend of both Pandavas and Kurus, even as Prajapati is friend of both gods and Asuras; 'as soon as thou goest thither, it will be accomplished.'
statements.evidence: MB 5.78 (pack), verbatim: 'foremost of all friends of both the Pandavas and the Kurus, even as Prajapati is of both the gods and the Asuras... As soon as thou goest thither, it will be accomplished.'

statements.claim: Arjuna said whatever Krishna wished — peace or war — the Pandavas would honour, and recalled that Duryodhana, unable to bear Yudhishthira's prosperity, had deprived them of their kingdom by deceitful dice.
statements.evidence: MB 5.78 (pack): 'Whether it be peace or war with the foe that thou wishest, any wish, O Krishna, that thou mayest entertain, will certainly be honoured by us'; 'deprived us of our kingdom by the sinful expedient of deceitful dice.'

statements.claim: Arjuna asked what bowman born in the Kshatriya order, invited to combat, would turn from the fight even if sure to die, and said he had thought Suyodhana deserved death since their sinful defeat and banishment to the woods.
statements.evidence: MB 5.78 (pack), verbatim: 'What bowman is there, who, born in the Kshatriya order, and invited to combat, turneth away from the fight even if he is sure to die?... even then... I thought that Suyodhana deserved death at my hands.'

statements.claim: If Krishna judged the Kauravas' immediate destruction preferable, let it be done soon; Krishna alone could walk the road of peace, related to both houses and trusted in both courts.
statements.evidence: MB 5.78 (pack): 'if thou deemest their immediate destruction to be preferable, let it be effected soon'; 5.78: Krishna is 'foremost of all friends of both the Pandavas and the Kurus' (kinship/trust gloss is consistent with 5.83's 'Related with both the parties').

statements.claim: Arjuna recalled how Draupadi was insulted in the assembly by Duryodhana and borne with patience, said wise counsels would be lost on Duryodhana like seed in barren soil, and asked Krishna to do without delay what he thought proper.
statements.evidence: MB 5.78 (pack), verbatim: 'how Draupadi was insulted in the midst of the assembly... Wise counsels will be lost on him like seed sown in a barren soil. Therefore, do without delay what thou... thinkest to be proper.'

notes: Pack evidence covers Arjuna's speech only (MB 5.78); the story's claim that Bhima and Nakula also spoke rests on the pack's own index summary and is left unquoted, so no fabricated content is asserted. 'For days the tent had argued' and the closing atmosphere are connective.

statements.claim: Arjuna told Krishna he was the best friend of all the Kurus, related to both parties, and competent to bring about peace and reconciliation between the Pandavas and Dhritarashtra's sons.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack): 'Thou art now, O Kesava, the best friend of all the Kurus. Related with both the parties... it behoveth thee to bring about peace between the Pandavas and the sons of Dhritarashtra.'

statements.claim: Arjuna asked Krishna to tell Suyodhana that if the foolish Duryodhana did not accept his auspicious counsels he would be the victim of his fate.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack), verbatim: 'say unto our ever-wrathful brother Suyodhana... If the foolish Duryodhana doth not accept thy auspicious and beneficial counsels... he will surely then be the victim of his fate.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered: 'Yes, I will go to king Dhritarashtra, desirous of accomplishing what is consistent with righteousness, what may be beneficial to us, and what also is for the good of the Kurus.'
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack), verbatim quote; also the pack excerpt.

statements.claim: The next morning was bright with the Maitra hour, the month Kartika under the constellation Revati, the season of dew after autumn, the earth covered with abundant crops.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack): 'a bright sun arose in the east. The hour called Maitra set in... The month was (Kaumuda Kartika) under the constellation Revati. It was the season of dew... The earth was covered with abundant crops.'

statements.claim: Krishna performed the morning rites — bath, unguents and ornaments, worship of Sun and Fire, touching a bull's tail, bowing to Brahmanas, walking round the sacred fire, viewing auspicious articles.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack): 'purified himself by a bath, and decked his person with unguents and ornaments, worshipped both the Sun and Fire. And having touched the tail of a bull and reverently bowed to the Brahmanas, walked round the sacred fire, and cast his eyes on the auspicious articles.'

statements.claim: Recollecting Yudhishthira's words, Krishna ordered Satyaki to ready his car with conch, discus, mace, quivers, darts and all weapons, since Duryodhana, Karna and Suvala's son were wicked and even contemptible foes should not be disregarded.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack), verbatim: 'Janardana recollected Yudhishthira's word and addressed... Satyaki... 'Let my car be made ready and let my conch and discus along with my mace, and quivers and darts and all kinds of weapons... be placed on it, for Duryodhana and Karna and Suvala's son are all of wicked souls.''

statements.claim: The chariot blazed like the fire of universal dissolution, matched the rider's speed, had wheels like sun and moon, emblazonments of moons/fishes/animals/birds, garlands, pearls and gems, a tall flagstaff with pennons and tiger-skins, and was yoked with Saivya, Sugriva, Meghapushpa and Valahaka; Garuda perched on the flagstaff with a terrible rattle.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack), detailed description matching all elements including the four named steeds and Garuda on the flagstaff.

statements.claim: Krishna mounted the car, high as Meru's summit and loud as kettle-drum or thunder, took Satyaki up beside him, and set out amid cloudless sky, auspicious winds, right-whirling auspicious animals and birds, cranes/peacocks/swans, and right-leaning homa-fed flames.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack), matching omens and portents descriptions.

statements.claim: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins, Chekitana, Dhrishtaketu of the Chedis, Drupada and the king of Kasi followed the car as Krishna set out for the residence of the Kurus.
statements.evidence: MB 5.83 (pack): 'Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, followed him, as also Bhima and Arjuna and... the twin sons of Madri. And the valiant Chekitana and Dhrishtaketu, the ruler of the Chedis, and Drupada and the king of Kasi...' (list continues in the truncated passage; 'Yudhishthira followed his cousin' is accurate — Yudhishthira and Krishna are cousins through Kunti/Vasudeva).

notes: Story extends through the departure narrative that the corpus's next story (DKS_0413, 'Krishna Prepares His Chariot and Sets Out for Hastinapura') is titled to cover — an editorial overlap, not a fidelity issue; every element is verbatim-grounded in MB 5.83. Closing 'accompanied... for a little way and then let it go' is connective.
